questions.q: What does the Five Whys technique accomplish?
options: It moves one layer deeper with each question, from a visible symptom toward something that's actually fixable, instead of stopping at the first answer
It requires asking exactly five unrelated questions about an incident
It replaces the need for any observability data during an investigation
It only applies to data quality issues, never pipeline-health issues
questions.explain: Stopping too early risks fixing only the immediate misconfiguration while leaving the real gap open for the same mistake to recur differently.

questions.q: Why does Lesson 52's observability data matter for root cause analysis?
options: It makes each "why" answerable with actual evidence — traces, logs, and metrics — instead of guessing
Observability data is irrelevant to root cause analysis
Only metrics are ever useful during a root cause investigation
Root cause analysis should rely purely on the incident responder's intuition
questions.explain: Root cause analysis without observability data is just speculation dressed up as an investigation.

questions.q: What distinguishes a root cause from a contributing factor?
options: A root cause is the earliest fixable point that would have prevented the whole chain; a contributing factor made the problem worse or more likely without causing it alone
They are the exact same thing with different names
A contributing factor is always more important to fix than the root cause
Symptoms and root causes are identical concepts
questions.explain: Fixing only a contributing factor or symptom leaves the actual root cause standing, ready to cause the next incident.

questions.q: Why does a blameless postmortem get better information than one focused on assigning blame?
options: Asking "what allowed this to happen" gets people volunteering the full, honest sequence of events, since nobody's defending themselves
Blameless postmortems are required by Fabric's own tooling
Assigning blame always produces more accurate technical detail
Blameless postmortems skip the Five Whys process entirely
questions.explain: Asking "who broke this" gets people minimizing what they did out of self-protection, which is understandable but unhelpful.

questions.q: In the Lesson 57 incident example, what was identified as the actual root cause, not just a contributing factor?
options: The CI/CD pipeline only validated notebooks and never validated Eventstream definitions
The Activator alert firing repeatedly
The Window transformation being misconfigured
The change being made directly in the prod workspace
questions.explain: This was the earliest fixable point — the missing CI check — that, if fixed, would have prevented the whole chain of events.
